first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the most tempting move, and memory_73 is the single most consequential-yet-weakly-underwritten belief for the stated objective: it records acquisition and revenue lift, which are short-horizon proxies, and says nothing about retention, discount-cohort LTV, or margin. Discount-acquired SMB accounts under competitive price pressure are exactly the cohort most likely to churn or repurchase only at the promo price, so a lift there can be negative for sustainable qualified revenue. That is why it is my first verification pull even though it is not my intended action — I want to know whether the archived record measured anything past the acquisition window before I let it pull the slot. My second pull is memory_86, the belief I actually intend to act on: it reports completion and adoption lift but stops short of revenue, so I need to see whether the original experiment tracked accounts through to paid/qualified conversion or only to time-to-value. The observed declines are concretely in onboarding (-4%) and activation (-6%), and memory_86, memory_31, and memory_91 all point the same direction, so simplify_onboarding attacks a measured internal regression rather than reacting to a competitor's pricing on their terms. Named downstream risk: 'cutting required fields' (memory_31) can raise raw activation while degrading lead qualification data and routing, converting a qualified-revenue objective into a volume objective — so the experiment must carry guardrails on qualified-lead rate, enterprise routing accuracy, and 60-day retention, not just completion rate. I did not verify memory_57 or memory_44 because referral and enterprise-assist are not contending for this slot, and memory_57 already carries an explicit retention check. If the memory_73 record turns out to include durable retention and margin evidence, promotional_pricing becomes a live contender and I would revisit before committing.

final.rationale: Verification resolved the key question. memory_73 was actively misleading as consolidated: exp_73 shows +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue but -12% 30-day retention, and the original record explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The consolidated memory had stripped that warning and kept only the favorable half. Against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, promotional_pricing is now disqualified rather than merely unattractive — matching the competitor's entry pricing would buy a cohort that does not survive its first renewal, which is the exact failure mode the objective is meant to exclude. memory_86 verified clean: +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and crucially +3% 30-day retention, so the adoption lift is not being paid for out of durability. That is the one candidate with direct evidence on the retention axis where the discount play failed. It also targets a measured internal regression (onboarding -4%, activation -6%) rather than reacting to a competitor's pricing on their chosen terms, and memory_31 and memory_91 point the same direction on the adjacent activation decline. Standard experiment scale is warranted because the mechanism is now verified on the axis that matters, not just on proxies. Residual uncertainty I am not collapsing: exp_86 measured retention at 30 days, which does not establish behavior through a full renewal cycle, and it does not report qualified-revenue conversion directly — so adoption-to-revenue transfer remains inferred, not shown. Named downstream risk carried forward: memory_31's mechanism is 'cutting required fields,' which can inflate raw activation while degrading lead qualification data and enterprise routing, quietly converting a qualified-revenue objective into a volume objective. Guardrails are therefore mandatory: qualified-lead rate, enterprise routing accuracy, and retention tracked to at least 60 days, with the experiment read as failed if completion rises while qualified-lead rate falls. memory_73 should be rewritten in durable memory to carry the retention loss and the original do-not-generalize conclusion, so the next agent does not inherit the stripped version and reach for discounting under the same pressure.
